issues.title: Nested-vector "no Go type" error blames the wrong cause
issues.verdictReason: Reproduced: unmarshalling a nested vector into *any hits marshal.go:1048's new guard and reports 'no Go type for element type', but asVectorType (helpers.go:77) strips the inner spec from the nested VectorType's custom name, so goType()/NewWithError() wrongly fail even though a real Go type ([]float32 etc.) exists for the element.
issues.scopeReason: The PR body explicitly lists this exact case as deferred work ('Out — making a nested vector actually decode into interface{} ... #1085'), and fixing the message requires the same asVectorType fix that issue tracks.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The nested-vector panic is turned into an error that says the element type has no Go type, even though one exists. The real cause is left in place: the inner vector's custom name is cut down to the bare "...VectorType" prefix.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: The nested-vector panic is turned into an error that says the element type has no Go type, even though one exists. The real cause is left in place: the inner vector's custom name is cut down to the bare "...VectorType" prefix.

issues.title: VectorType has no String(), so vector errors render uninformatively
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed no VectorType.String() exists; it inherits NativeType.String(), which for a nested vector's bare custom name renders only 'custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)' with no element type or dimension, verified with a small reproduction.
issues.scopeReason: Improving what the new error prints is independent of the deeper decode-support fix deferred to #1085, and the error text itself is new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: For the nested-vector case the new error cannot say which type the server sent. VectorType has no String method, so %v of the inner VectorType uses NativeType.String and renders "custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)", with no element type or dimension.

issues.title: Function comment overclaims that every unmarshalVector path allocates
issues.verdictReason: vectorSliceReuse (marshal.go:941) reuses the destination slice without allocating when capacity suffices, and the array branch (around marshal.go:1078) never calls make/reflect.MakeSlice, contradicting the new comment's blanket 'every path below turns it into an allocation' claim.
issues.scopeReason: The inaccurate comment is new text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The function-level comment says "every path below turns it into an allocation (make, reflect.MakeSlice)". That is not true for the array destination, or for vectorSliceReuse when the destination already has enough capacity. The PR's own test comment contradicts it.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize floors a 0-dim fixed-type nested vector at 1, not 0
issues.verdictReason: Reproduced: unmarshalVector on vector<vector<float,0>,5> with an empty, non-NULL payload now errors '5 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes', although a 0-dimension vector of a fixed-size element type legitimately encodes to 0 bytes and used to decode successfully; the new test comments ('Neither can describe an element in zero bytes', 'never encoded in fewer than N bytes') assert this wrong floor as fact instead of flagging it.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize is new code added by this PR, and the decode regression and the test/doc claims about it are new.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 for a fixed-element inner vector with 0 dimensions, but such an element really takes 0 bytes on the wire. A vector<vector<float,0>,N> with an empty non-NULL payload used to decode and is now rejected. Related: the TestVectorElemMinSize and TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads comments assert the bound is a correct floor / non-narrowing when it is not for this case.

issues.title: Negative-dimension check runs before NULL check, splitting *[]T vs **[]T
issues.verdictReason: Reproduced: Unmarshal on a NULL vector value with Dimensions=-3 now errors for a *[]float32 destination, but still returns nil for a **[]float32 destination, because isNullableValue/unmarshalNullable short-circuits on nil data before ever calling unmarshalVector, bypassing the new Dimensions<0 check entirely for double-pointer destinations.
issues.scopeReason: The new Dimensions<0 check, which now runs ahead of the data==nil case for single-pointer destinations, is new code from this PR, and the inconsistency it creates isn't mentioned in the PR's behaviour-change notes.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A NULL value for a vector column with negative metadata dimensions now errors for a `*[]T` destination but still succeeds for a `**[]T` destination; the negative-dimension check runs before the NULL check. The PR's behaviour-change section does not mention this.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-parallel-broker-2026-10-08: A NULL value for a vector column with negative metadata dimensions now errors for a `*[]T` destination but still succeeds for a `**[]T` destination; the negative-dimension check runs before the NULL check. issues.title: getCassandraLongType's custom-name change isn't scoped to vectors only
issues.verdictReason: getCassandraLongType is the shared recursive parser for set/list/map/tuple/UDT/frozen/vector element names (7 call sites found via grep), so the new branch that preserves an unrecognized name onto a CustomType changes TypeInfo for every unrecognized basic type name throughout metadata parsing, not only vector elements, which the PR's 'Behaviour change' section doesn't mention.
issues.scopeReason: This is the exact diff hunk added by the PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The getCassandraLongType change applies to every unrecognised type name in all metadata parsing, not only to vector elements. The PR's 'Behaviour change' section does not mention it.
